hooks.text: In 1907, inspectors measured a bending steel chord on the Quebec Bridge.
Why did engineers ignore the bending steel on a massive bridge?
A giant bridge was built even as its steel chords bent.

title: Why Did Engineers Ignore This Bending Steel? ⚠️
description: In 1907, inspectors on the Quebec Bridge measured a bending steel chord days before its collapse, but work continued until the disaster struck.

beats.text: In 1907, inspectors measured a bending steel chord on the Quebec Bridge.
beats.visual: photograph of the Quebec Bridge under construction, 1907

beats.text: Designing engineer Peter Szlapka drafted the lower chords with a defective design.
beats.visual: portrait of designing engineer Peter Szlapka

beats.text: Consulting engineer Theodore Cooper officially approved these flawed plans.
beats.visual: portrait of consulting engineer Theodore Cooper

beats.text: Officials placed complete confidence in Cooper's judgment.
beats.visual: photograph of bridge construction workers and officials, 1907

beats.text: But contemporary professional knowledge of steel columns under load was inadequate.
beats.visual: technical drawing of the Quebec Bridge cantilever design

beats.text: By August 27, no action could prevent the structural collapse.
beats.visual: photograph of the collapsed ruins of the Quebec Bridge in the river, 1907

beats.text: Yet better judgment could have saved human lives on the site.
beats.visual: photograph of a newspaper front page reporting the 1907 disaster
